research_rationale: EO 10352 (signed 1952-05-19; 17 FR 4607, filed 1952-05-20, printed in the Federal Register of 1952-05-21) has one operative paragraph: it amends section 6.10-1 of 33 CFR Part 6 (the regulations prescribed by EO 10173 as amended by EO 10277) to read as the order sets out. The held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10352.txt was read in full and its identity (number, title, date, signer, FR page) matches the register row. The order states no effective date other than its signing, no own-terms end and no savings clause. I searched the held texts for the order's number: later orders EO 11249 (1965-10-10), EO 13143 (1999-12-01), EO 13273 (2002-08-21) and EO 14116 (2024-02-21) amend other sections of 33 CFR Part 6 (11249: 6.01-3, 6.01-4, new 6.01-5, 6.04-5, new 6.04-6, 6.04-7; 13143: 6.01-4; 13273: new 6.01-6 and 6.04-1; 14116: 6.01-3, 6.01-5, new sections after 6.01-6 and 6.01-7, 6.04-5 through 6.04-8, 6.10-7, 6.14-1 and later sections) and none amends, supersedes or revokes section 6.10-1 or EO 10352. The Federal Register disposition note for EO 10352 reads 'See: EO 11249, October 10, 1965' and EO 11249 recites EO 10352 only in its preamble. The current-law machine searches (U.S. Code release point 119-121 current through 2026-10-09, so laws enacted from 2026-10-10 to 2026-10-14 are not reflected; eCFR as of 2026-10-14) were read for coverage; the eCFR hits are 33 CFR 6.10-1, 33 CFR part 125 and 29 CFR 1915.2, and the held eCFR text of 33 CFR 6.10-1 (jobs/theophilus-sources/output/texts/cfr-t33-6.10-1.txt) still carries the same sentence as the order, with the source line '[E.O. 10352, 17 FR 4624, May 21, 1952]' (that citation is the Coast Guard implementing page, the order itself is at 17 FR 4607). No revocation of EO 10352, EO 10173 or Part 6 appears in the held sources.

independent_command_check: There is one command only, the replacement text of 33 CFR 6.10-1; no independent command survives separately from it.

research_rationale: EO 11190 (signed 1964-12-29; 29 FR 19183, filed 1964-12-30, printed 1964-12-31) has two operative sections: section 1 delegates to the Secretary of Defense (and, for the Coast Guard, to a second Secretary) the President's authority under section 271 of title 10, U.S. Code, to prescribe regulations for screening the Ready Reserve; section 2 revokes EO 10651 of January 6, 1956. I read the held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11190.txt in full; number, title, signer and FR page match the register row (the OCR of the signing date line is garbled; the register and the FR citation give 1964-12-29). Later instruments naming the order: EO 11382 (signed 1967-11-28, 32 FR 16247) strikes out the Secretary of the Treasury and inserts the Secretary of Transportation in this order (it lists EO 11190 among the orders so amended), and EO 13286 section 67 (signed 2003-02-28, 68 FR 10619; effective March 1, 2003 under its section 92) strikes the Secretary of Transportation in section 1 and inserts the Secretary of Homeland Security. research_rationale: EO 12403 (signed 1983-02-08, Ronald Reagan; 48 FR 6087, printed in the Federal Register of 1983-02-10) has three operative sections: section 1 designates the African Development Bank under the International Organizations Immunities Act, section 2 amends EO 11269 sections 2(c), 3(d) and 7 to add the Bank to the lists of institutions, and section 3 delegates to the Secretary of the Treasury the President's functions under four sections of Public Law 97-35. Kennedy; 26 FR 11714; filed 1961-12-06 per the Federal Register document line) establishes an award program for contributions to the Export Expansion Program: section 1 establishes it, section 2 directs the Secretary of Commerce to set nomination and granting procedures, section 3 names the President's E Award and the E Certificate of Service, section 4 and 5 describe the two awards, and section 6 allows recipients to issue a pin and use the emblem. I read the held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10978.txt in full (identity matches the register row: number, title, date, signer, page 11714) and the prepared inventory of eight clauses covers every numbered section and subsection of it (the preamble recitals are not operative). The order has no duration, condition or deadline. The bounded machine searches were read for coverage: the U.S. Code search (release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09; laws enacted 2026-10-10 to 2026-10-14 are not reflected), the eCFR search (as of 2026-10-14) and the Federal Register disposition-note search (6941 catalog records) each returned zero hits naming this order, so no amendment, revocation or supersession is recorded in any of them. The held texts that cite the order's number are the 1989 codification snapshot, the order itself and a 2011 Federal Register notice from the Department of Commerce, which describes the E Award Program as established by the order; none ends it. No later instrument is held that affects the order, so the legal predicate for continuation is the held original read with those bounded searches (the original_plus_bounded_search route); this is evidence of absence of an ending in the searched sources, not a positive 2026 source, and I state it so.
